item_name: Hemiplegia or Hemiparesis (Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days)

lookback_source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

lookback_notes: Two look-back periods are stated for this section and both apply to I4900: diagnosis identification (Step 1) uses a 60-day look-back ("physician-documented diagnosis ... in the last 60 days", p. I-8), and diagnosis status active/inactive (Step 2) uses a 7-day look-back (p. I-8). The assessor's observation window for determining whether the diagnosis is active is 7 days, so lookback_days = 7. Per the general convention, the ARD is day 1 of the look-back period and a 7-day window is the ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-21); the item's own pages do not restate how the days are counted. The 30-day exception stated on pp. I-9/I-14 applies only to Item I2300 (UTI), not to I4900.

coding_levels.label: I4900 Hemiplegia or Hemiparesis — checked
coding_levels.definition: Check I4900 when hemiplegia or hemiparesis is a disease with a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days that has a direct relationship to the resident's current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Code diseases that have a documented diagnosis in the last 60 days and have a direct relationship to the resident’s current functional status, cognitive status, mood or behavior status, medical treatments, nursing monitoring, or risk of death during the 7-day look-back period

coding_levels.label: I4900 — left blank (not an active diagnosis)
coding_levels.definition: Leave the box blank when the condition does not meet the active-diagnosis criteria; per the general convention, check-all-that-apply boxes remain blank if the specified condition is not met.

source.quote: Use a check mark for boxes where the instructions state to "check all that apply," if the specified condition is met; otherwise, these boxes should remain blank

federal_coding_rules.rule: I4900 captures hemiplegia or hemiparesis, listed under the Neurological disease category of Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

source.quote: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident's current status, or do not drive the resident's plan of care during the 7-day look-back period; these are inactive diagnoses.

source.quote: Do not include conditions that have been resolved, do not affect the resident’s current status, or do not drive the resident’s plan of care during the 7-day look-back period, as these would be considered inactive diagnoses.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Check off each active disease; check all that apply.

source.quote: Check off each active disease. Check all that apply.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Examples of diseases included for a disease category are not exhaustive; diseases coded in these categories are not limited to only those listed in the examples.

source.quote: Examples of diseases are included for some disease categories. Diseases to be coded in these categories are not meant to be limited to only those listed in the examples.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a disease or condition is not specifically listed, enter the diagnosis and ICD code in item I8000, Additional active diagnosis.

source.quote: If a disease or condition is not specifically listed, enter the diagnosis and ICD code in item I8000, Additional active diagnosis.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If no listed condition is an active diagnosis, code I7900, none of the above active diagnoses within the past 7 days.

source.quote: I7900, none of the above active diagnoses within the past 7 days

federal_coding_rules.rule: For individuals with severe physical disabilities where there is minimal ability for purposeful movement, the primary physician-documented diagnosis should be coded on the MDS and not the resulting paralysis or paresis from that condition (stated in the coding tip for Item I5100 Quadriplegia; e.g., cerebral palsy with spastic quadriplegia is coded in I4400, not I5100).

source.quote: For individuals with these types of severe physical disabilities, where there is minimal ability for purposeful movement, their primary physician-documented diagnosis should be coded on the MDS and not the resulting paralysis or paresis from that condition.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the primary medical condition category coded in I0020B applies, it must also be included in items I0100–I8000: Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

source.quote: Include the primary medical condition coded in item I0020B in items I0100–I8000: Active Diagnoses in the Last 7 Days.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Where a practitioner has potentially misdiagnosed a resident with a condition for which there is a lack of appropriate diagnostic information in the medical record, the corresponding diagnosis in Section I should not be coded.

source.quote: the corresponding diagnosis in Section I should not be coded, and a referral by the facility and/or the survey team to the State Medical Boards or Boards of Nursing may be necessary.

federal.criterion: A physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) of hemiplegia or hemiparesis within the last 60 days must exist in the medical record.

source.quote: The disease conditions in this section require a physician-documented diagnosis (or by a nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist if allowable under state licensure laws) in the last 60 days.

federal.notes: Step 1 of the two-step assessment process.

federal.criterion: Acceptable medical record sources for physician diagnoses: progress notes, most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, diagnosis/problem list, and other resources as available; if a diagnosis/problem list is used, only diagnoses confirmed by the physician should be entered.

source.quote: Medical record sources for physician diagnoses include progress notes, the most recent history and physical, transfer documents, discharge summaries, diagnosis/ problem list, and other resources as available. If a diagnosis/problem list is used, only diagnoses confirmed by the physician should be entered.

federal.criterion: Diagnoses communicated verbally must be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure follow-up.

source.quote: it is also essential that diagnoses communicated verbally be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure follow-up.

federal.criterion: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must also be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure validity and follow-up.

source.quote: Diagnostic information, including past history obtained from family members and close contacts, must also be documented in the medical record by the physician to ensure validity and follow-up.

federal.criterion: Check these medical record sources for the last 7 days to identify "active" diagnoses: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor's orders, consults and official diagnostic reports, and other sources as available.

source.quote: Check the following information sources in the medical record for the last 7 days to identify “active” diagnoses: transfer documents, physician progress notes, recent history and physical, recent discharge summaries, nursing assessments, nursing care plans, medication sheets, doctor’s orders, consults and official diagnostic reports, and other sources as available.

federal.criterion: Specific physician (or NP/PA/CNS) documentation that the condition is active is sufficient documentation of active disease and requires no additional confirmation; such documentation may be found in progress notes, most recent history and physical, transfer notes, hospital discharge summary, etc.

source.quote: There may be specific documentation in the medical record by a physician, nurse practitioner, physician assistant, or clinical nurse specialist of active diagnosis.

federal.notes: Framed as a Coding Tip indicator.

federal.criterion: In the absence of specific documentation that the disease is active, active disease may be confirmed by recent onset or acute exacerbation indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms, and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days (sources may include radiological reports, hospital discharge summaries, doctor's orders).

source.quote: Recent onset or acute exacerbation of the disease or condition indicated by a positive study, test or procedure, hospitalization for acute symptoms and/or recent change in therapy in the last 7 days.

federal.notes: Listed as an indicator that "may be used" to confirm active disease.

federal.criterion: Symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days may confirm active disease; a symptom must be specifically attributed to the disease (sources may include radiological reports, nursing assessments and care plans, progress notes).

source.quote: Symptoms and abnormal signs indicating ongoing or decompensated disease in the last 7 days.

federal.criterion: Listing a disease/diagnosis on the resident's medical record problem list is not sufficient for determining active or inactive status; the reviewer would check progress notes (including the history and physical) during the 7-day look-back period for treatment of symptoms, doctor's orders for medications, and documentation of physical or other therapy for functional limitations caused by the condition.

source.quote: Listing a disease/diagnosis (e.g., arthritis) on the resident’s medical record problem list is not sufficient for determining active or inactive status.

federal.criterion: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions to manage a condition that requires monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or for potentially severe side effects in the last 7 days indicates active disease; monitoring of medications for adverse effects alone relates to management of pharmacotherapy, not to management or monitoring of the underlying disease.

source.quote: Ongoing therapy with medications or other interventions to manage a condition that requires monitoring for therapeutic efficacy or to monitor potentially severe side effects in the last 7 days.

federal.notes: Second bullet on p. I-14 clarifies that routine adverse-effect monitoring does not by itself establish active disease.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The pages for Section I active diagnoses do not tie I4900 to any payment or case-mix classification. (I0020 references the Medicare Part A stay, but that is a separate item and no case-mix/payment group is stated for I4900.)

conflicts.topic: Coexistence of a 60-day and a 7-day look-back window for this section

positions.claim: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) uses a 60-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis identification (Step 1) is a 60-day look-back period.

positions.claim: Diagnosis status: active or inactive (Step 2) uses a 7-day look-back period.

source.quote: Diagnosis status: Active or Inactive (Step 2) is a 7-day look-back period (except for Item I2300 UTI, which does not use the active 7-day look-back period).

conflicts.resolution: Resolved by the document itself: it explicitly states "There are two look-back periods for this section" — 60 days for identifying a physician-documented diagnosis and 7 days for determining that the diagnosis is active (p. I-8, reiterated in the Coding Instructions on p. I-9).
